root_idea.summary: The supplied lexical evidence centers on the lip as the mouth's visible covering, with extensions to direct mouth-to-mouth speech, approach, speaking, thirst, and depletion through many users or seekers.
root_idea.development: The bodily sense develops into Form III expressions for placing the lip near another and speaking directly, while further idiomatic extensions concern words, reputation, begging, water, food, and property consumed or reduced through use.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole Quran occurrence is the inflected dual شَفَتَيْنِ, which is presented under the normalized singular dictionary citation form شَفَةٌ.

senses.definition: A lip, the fleshy covering of the mouth; in the Quran, the pair of lips.
senses.usage_conditions: The attested Quran form is the dual شَفَتَيْنِ, “two lips.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike someone on the lip.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I transitive usage with the lip as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be used up or reduced through many drinkers, eaters, or seekers; said of water, food, or property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive or consequential usage in which numerous users or seekers result in diminished quantity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To importune someone by begging until his possessions are consumed; in the passive, to have one's possessions consumed by beggars.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes begging and its depletion of the possessor's property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To occupy or engage so as to divert from something; of the use of pasture or water, to keep it from another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage expresses diversion or withholding through one's occupation or use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put one's lip near another's; hence, to speak directly mouth-to-mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III construction used literally for lip-to-lip contact and conventionally for direct oral speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw near or approach a town, country, or affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of coming near, applied to places and affairs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lip-like part, metaphorically the lip of a horse or a bucket.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metaphorical extension of the bodily sense to analogous projecting or enclosing parts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In أَهْلُ الشَّفَةِ, those entitled to drink with their lips at a water source and to water their beasts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression concerning rights of access to drinking water.
Used in expressions such as بِنْتُ شَفَةٍ and ذَاتُ شَفَةٍ, especially in statements about speaking or hearing no word.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In خَفِيفُ الشَّفَةِ, one who asks or begs little; the expression is also reported for one who begs much.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional idiom with two opposing attested interpretations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person's report or reputation, or the people's speaking of that person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions describing favorable or unfavorable public mention and reputation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Labial; pertaining to the lips, especially letters articulated at the lips.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational and phonetic term; the cited labial letters include ب، ف، and م.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thick-lipped or large in the lips.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited usage applies the adjective to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thirsty, lacking enough water to moisten the lip.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a person in need of sufficient water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Much sought or used by many and consequently reduced or scarce; said of water, food, or property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Of water, it may have many drinkers or be sought or restricted because scarce; of food, it has many eaters; of property, it has many seekers or has become little in quantity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a person, having possessions consumed by much begging or by household members and guests.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial usage describing property exhausted through importunity or domestic consumption.
